title: Toolchain guard: stable state binding and re-entrant call suppression
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a runtime-level guard that establishes and enforces a stable execution snapshot for multi-tool chains, preventing accidental result re-injection and runaway recursion while preserving streaming semantics and structured output contracts.
background: We have recurring incidents and flaky behaviors when model-driven orchestrations perform multi-tool calls in a single request: tools mutate ephemeral execution context, LLM responses reinject previous tool outputs causing duplication, and naive loop detection either kills legitimate iterative chains or breaks streaming. Existing tickets explored loop quarantine and recursion throttles but did not define a compact, implementable invariant that works with streaming and function/tool calling APIs.
goals: Define a lightweight execution invariant that marks which state is considered immutable for the duration of a request
Ensure tool outputs can be injected to downstream steps exactly once unless explicitly permitted
Detect and suppress re-entrant calls that indicate a recursion loop while allowing bounded iterative patterns
Maintain compatibility with streaming token emission and structured output envelopes
Minimize latency/regression risk for existing users and provide clear opt-ins for advanced behaviors
non_goals: Replacing high-level orchestration frameworks (this is runtime-safety, not a choreography DSL)
Automated semantic verification of tool outputs (out of scope for this ticket)
Large-scale refactor of the kernel scheduler; we will hook into existing execution paths
proposal: Create a per-request 'execution snapshot' object (opaque ID + small metadata) that binds initial inputs, tool invocation provenance markers, and a monotonic injection index. Runtime enforces: 1) tool results are accepted only if their provenance marker matches the active snapshot or an allowed transitive snapshot; 2) any attempt to inject a tool result with an index lower than or equal to a previously applied injection is rejected to prevent duplication; 3) detect patterns of repeated injection cycles (>= N attempts within a sliding window) and convert the request into a guarded fallback path (return a structured error with diagnostics), while allowing a bounded iterative mode when request sets explicit iteration_count and iteration_whitelist flags.
implementation_notes: Add small snapshot table (in-memory map) keyed by request-id -> snapshot-id, with TTL matching request lifetime
Patch tool runner accept() path to require current snapshot-id and injection-index checks before mutating the request context
Expose opt-in request headers: X-Iteration-Mode, X-Iteration-Limit, X-Allow-Reinjection for backward compatibility
Streaming: buffer and tag streamed chunks with snapshot-id and injection-index metadata; do not emit downstream until a chunk's snapshot matches active snapshot to avoid racey replays
Provide a metrics surface: reinjection_attempts, reinjection_rejections, recursion_fallbacks, avg-injection-latency
Keep changes behind runtime feature flag 'toolchain_stable_bind' for staged rollout
decisions: Use opaque snapshot IDs (UUIDv4) rather than complex provenance graphs to minimize serialization overhead
Reject duplicate injection attempts deterministically rather than attempt auto-merge to preserve correctness
Allow bounded iteration only via explicit request flags to avoid surprising behavior for existing customers
Require streaming chunks to carry minimal metadata; avoid changing public API shape (use headers/metadata wrapper)
tradeoffs: Strict deduplication reduces surprising duplicates but can surface errors earlier, potentially requiring callers to modify orchestration logic
Adding snapshot lookups adds a tiny critical-path latency (microseconds) but prevents costly downstream retries and debugging time
Opt-in iteration mode keeps current behavior stable for existing users but places responsibility on caller to opt-in for iterative patterns
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests covering: single tool chain normal flow, duplicated injection rejected, allowed explicit reinjection succeeds
Integration test: streaming generator emits with correct snapshot metadata and client observes no duplicated chunks when reinjection is attempted
Load test: enabling feature flag does not increase median request latency by >3% on p99 token-heavy workloads
Observability: new metrics are emitted and dashboards created for reinjection_rejections and recursion_fallbacks
Confluence design doc and SDK compatibility notes published
testing_plan: Local harness: augment existing tool-runner test suite with snapshot fixture and simulated racey tool callbacks
E2E: create a synthetic orchestrator that deliberately tries to reinject same result multiple times and assert rejection and graceful fallback
Chaos: run within canary fleet with synthetic traffic that includes iterative patterns to validate iteration opt-in behavior
Compatibility: run SDK integration tests (Python/JS) verifying headers are passed through and streaming clients can handle annotated chunks
rollout_plan: Phase 1: merge behind feature flag; integration tests green; internal canary (10% of runtime requests) for 48 hours
Phase 2: expose opt-in header docs; invite a handful of partners to try iteration mode; monitor metrics and error budget impact for 7 days
Phase 3: default-enable for new requests while keeping control plane toggle to disable per-tenant if regressions occur
Phase 4: bake into public runtime release runtime-2.3 and update SDK changelogs
monitoring: reinjection_attempts: counter tagged by tenant, request-type
reinjection_rejections: counter with alert when rate > 0.1% of requests for a tenant
recursion_fallbacks: counter and example request snapshots (redacted) stored for triage
avg-injection-latency: histogram to detect perf regressions
dashboard: per-route panels showing reinjection rate, rejection rate, and p99 latency
dependencies: ENG-60123 (KV sanitization) - for context mutation boundaries
runtime-team library: request-metadata primitives (internal API change)
